name: Messina router hop() recursive VAA re-emission (Opulous OPUL)
summary: The Messina router on Avalanche, the Wormhole emitter trusted by every destination bridge, re-publishes any verified VAA through hop() without checking its emitter, source/destination network or target chain. Attackers fed the router's own output VAAs back into hop() hundreds of times, turning single deposits into many distinct claimable VAAs that released OPUL and other escrowed tokens on Arbitrum, Ethereum, BSC, Base and Polygon.
notes: Latest pre-exploit Upgraded event installed the router implementation whose hop() re-emits self-emitted and same-network VAAs.

Merged campaigns 2026-03-13/14 (Ethereum, BSC, Arbitrum), 03-24/25 (DBD, 0x53b8eba7), 03-30 (BUBBLE, 0x7e358874), 05-07 (Mog/BOBO, 0x6551de33) and 09-22 (BUBBLE/RLB/DEGEN, 0xe33112d9) against the same router implementation. Liquid escrowed assets are measured as escrow releases to the attacker set minus attacker deposits into the same escrow, at incident price. OPUL is an unbacked float on each chain and was dumped with large price impact, so it, BOBO, DBD and the September BUBBLE are valued only by realised DEX proceeds net of attacker purchases; roughly 80M OPUL sent to exchange deposit addresses or left unsold is not valued, so the figure is an onchain lower bound. Treasury fees are excluded and later recoveries are not deducted.
OPUL sent to exchange deposit addresses or retained (about 80M across Arbitrum and Ethereum) has no onchain disposal and is not valued; the loss is an onchain lower bound.

The EIP-1967 slot still selects the same implementation at Avalanche block 96340251 and hop() was not disabled; campaigns after the scanned range (router txlist through block 95906406, redemption logs through each chain's head on 2026-09-28) are not included.
The router implementation source is unverified; the failure identity is established from the traced call path, decoded calldata, storage diff and replay behaviour recorded in source-7.
